```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
devtools::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
chanwe_load_fonts()
# Quarto's fig-format resets knitr's dev to plain png (quartz on macOS),
# which cannot see systemfonts-registered families — re-assert ragg here.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png", dev.args = list(bg = "transparent"))

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(42)

# ── data ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mt <- tibble::as_tibble(mtcars, rownames = "model") |>
    mutate(
        cyl = factor(cyl),
        gear = factor(gear),
        am = factor(am, labels = c("Automatic", "Manual")),
        hp_band = cut(
            hp,
            breaks = c(-Inf, 110, 180, Inf),
            labels = c("Low", "Mid", "High")
        )
    )

econ <- economics |>
    filter(date >= as.Date("2000-01-01")) |>
    mutate(unemp_pct = unemploy / pop * 100)

deltas <- tibble::tibble(
    metric = c(
        "Revenue",
        "Gross margin",
        "EBITDA",
        "Opex",
        "Net income",
        "Churn"
    ),
    actual = c(1240.5, 682.1, 310.2, -420.3, 185.7, 42.0),
    qoq = c(12.4, 4.2, -3.1, -1.9, 5.8, -0.8),
    yoy = c(28.1, 9.6, 11.2, 6.3, -2.4, -4.1)
)

months <- seq(as.Date("2025-09-01"), by = "month", length.out = 12)
rev_df <- expand.grid(
    month = months,
    segment = c("Retail", "Wholesale", "Online"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
    arrange(segment, month) |>
    group_by(segment) |>
    mutate(
        revenue = round(
            c(Retail = 18, Wholesale = 12, Online = 7)[segment] +
                cumsum(rnorm(12, 0.6, 1.1)),
            2
        )
    ) |>
    ungroup()
spread_labels <- function(y, gap) {
    o <- order(y)
    ys <- y[o]
    for (i in seq_along(ys)[-1]) {
        if (ys[i] - ys[i - 1] < gap) ys[i] <- ys[i - 1] + gap
    }
    y[o] <- ys
    y
}
rev_last <- rev_df |>
    group_by(segment) |>
    slice_max(month, n = 1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(y_lab = spread_labels(revenue, 1.5))

cyl_summary <- mt |>
    group_by(cyl) |>
    summarise(
        avg_mpg = mean(mpg),
        avg_hp = mean(hp),
        avg_wt = mean(wt),
        sd_mpg = sd(mpg),
        n = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
    )

region_rev <- tibble::tibble(
    region = c("North", "Center", "West", "South", "Total"),
    q1 = c(412.1, 388.4, 251.9, 188.1, 1240.5),
    q2 = c(438.0, 371.2, 266.3, 201.5, 1277.0),
    delta = c(6.3, -4.4, 5.7, 7.1, 2.9)
)

heat <- expand.grid(week = 1:12, region = c("North", "Center", "West", "South"))
heat$delta <- round(
    rnorm(nrow(heat), 0, 2) + rep(c(1.4, 0.3, -0.6, -1.5), each = 12),
    1
)
heat_m <- max(abs(heat$delta))

fleet8 <- mt |> select(model, mpg, cyl, hp, wt) |> slice_head(n = 8)
fmt_fleet <- list(
    mpg = \(x) formatC(x, digits = 2, format = "f"),
    hp = \(x) formatC(x, digits = 0, format = "d"),
    wt = \(x) formatC(x, digits = 2, format = "f")
)

# ── reusable pieces ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
chart <- chanwe_palette("chart")

kpi_reserves <- chanwe_kpi(
    num = "45,91",
    label = "USD MM",
    period = "05·MAY·2026",
    mtc1_num = "0,19%",
    mtc1_label = "WoW",
    mtc1_direction = "+",
    mtc2_num = "3,17%",
    mtc2_label = "MoM",
    mtc2_direction = "-",
    mtc3_num = "17,78%",
    mtc3_label = "YoY",
    mtc3_direction = "+"
)

# base scatter used across the header / surface sections
p_fleet <- ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = hp_band)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.88) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_color_chanwe_d() +
    labs(
        x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
        y = "Miles per gallon",
        color = "HP band",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: Motor Trend, 1974")
    )
```

# The Color System

Every color in `chanwer` is a named token. `chanwe_palette()` returns the
full inventory; `chanwe_palette("<group>")` returns one group;
`chanwe_preview_palette("<group>")` draws its swatch grid.

::: {.chanwe-callout kind="note" eyebrow="BRAND ROLES" title="The manual assigns each family a job"}
Coral is the house lead, blue is structural, green is positive, vermillion
is alert, ink is the neutral anchor. The scales below are built on those
roles — positive/negative is never an arbitrary red/green pair.
:::

## The categorical eight

Fixed, CVD-validated slot order — coral, blue, teal, green, violet,
magenta, mustard, ink. Mustard and ink sit last deliberately: charts with
up to six series never reach them.

```{r}
#| label: preview-chart
#| fig-height: 3.4
chanwe_preview_palette("chart")
```

## The signed trio

Hue-true darkenings of the brand's positive (green), alert (vermillion)
and neutral (ink) families, stepped until each passes WCAG 4.5:1
small-text contrast on all five brand surfaces.

```{r}
#| label: preview-signed
#| fig-height: 2.4
chanwe_preview_palette("signed")
```

## Semantic roles and family ramps

```{r}
#| label: preview-semantic
#| fig-height: 3.4
chanwe_preview_palette("semantic")
```

# Scales

## Categorical

`scale_color_chanwe_d()` / `scale_fill_chanwe_d()` assign the chart
palette in slot order, recycling past eight.

```{r}
#| label: cat-scatter
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = am)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_color_chanwe_d() +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Fuel economy by weight",
            eyebrow = "CATEGORICAL - 2 SERIES"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Nominal series only - scatter charts stay at three or fewer"
        ),
        x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
        y = "MPG",
        color = "Transmission",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

::: {.chanwe-callout kind="warning" eyebrow="SERIES CAP" title="Scatter, bubble, and maps: three series maximum"}
In those forms any two marks can sit side by side, so the palette must
pass the stricter all-pairs check — the first three slots do. Fold extra
series into "Other" or facet. Bars, lines, and stacks may use up to six.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cat-bars
#| fig-height: 4.2
mpg_drv <- ggplot2::mpg |>
    mutate(
        drv = factor(
            drv,
            levels = c("f", "4", "r"),
            labels = c("Front", "4WD", "Rear")
        ),
        class = reorder(class, class, FUN = length)
    )
ggplot(mpg_drv, aes(y = class, fill = drv)) +
    geom_bar(width = 0.62) +
    scale_fill_chanwe_d() +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Vehicles by class and drivetrain",
            eyebrow = "CATEGORICAL - STACKED BARS"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Color encodes a second nominal variable - bars and stacks may use up to six series"
        ),
        x = "Vehicles",
        y = NULL,
        fill = "Drivetrain",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::mpg")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

## Ordinal: one-hue ramp

When category order carries meaning, use a ramp group so the reader sees
the order in the color: `scale_fill_chanwe_d(palette = "p15_blue", reverse = TRUE)`.

```{r}
#| label: ordinal
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(hp_band, fill = hp_band)) +
    geom_bar(width = 0.55) +
    scale_fill_chanwe_d(palette = "p15_blue", reverse = TRUE) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Fleet by horsepower band",
            eyebrow = "ORDINAL - ONE HUE"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Low to High reads light to dark in a single family"
        ),
        x = NULL,
        y = "Vehicles",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(legend_position = "none")
```

## Sequential

`scale_color_chanwe_c()` / `scale_fill_chanwe_c()` encode magnitude with
one-hue, light-to-dark brand gradients: `orange` (default), `coral`,
`blue`, `teal`, `green`, `vermillion`, `magenta`, `violet`, `mustard`,
`ink`.

```{r}
#| label: seq-teal
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = disp)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.8) +
    scale_color_chanwe_c(palette = "teal") +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Displacement gradient",
            eyebrow = "SEQUENTIAL - TEAL"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("One hue, light to dark, magnitude only"),
        x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
        y = "MPG",
        color = "Disp.",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

```{r}
#| label: seq-orange
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(econ, aes(date, unemp_pct, color = psavert)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_color_chanwe_c() +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Unemployment, colored by savings rate",
            eyebrow = "SEQUENTIAL - ORANGE (DEFAULT)"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "The default gradient anchors on the report primary"
        ),
        x = NULL,
        y = "Unemployment (%)",
        color = "Savings %",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::economics")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

## Diverging

`scale_fill_chanwe_div()` encodes polarity — vermillion through a neutral
midpoint to green, signed tokens at the poles. Give it symmetric limits so
zero lands on the midpoint.

```{r}
#| label: div-heat
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(heat, aes(week, region, fill = delta)) +
    geom_tile(
        color = chanwe_palette("core")[["brand-white"]],
        linewidth = 1.2
    ) +
    scale_fill_chanwe_div(limits = c(-heat_m, heat_m)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2, 12, by = 2)) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Weekly delta vs plan",
            eyebrow = "DIVERGING - HEATMAP"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Symmetric limits pin zero to the neutral midpoint"
        ),
        x = "Week",
        y = NULL,
        fill = "Δ pp",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: simulated")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

```{r}
#| label: div-heat-cvd
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(heat, aes(week, region, fill = delta)) +
    geom_tile(
        color = chanwe_palette("core")[["brand-white"]],
        linewidth = 1.2
    ) +
    scale_fill_chanwe_div(limits = c(-heat_m, heat_m), cvd = TRUE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2, 12, by = 2)) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Weekly delta vs plan, CVD-safe",
            eyebrow = "DIVERGING - CVD = TRUE"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Positive arm switches to structural blue; polarity survives deuteranopia"
        ),
        x = "Week",
        y = NULL,
        fill = "Δ pp",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: simulated")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

```{r}
#| label: div-bars
#| fig-height: 4.2
mk <- ggplot2::mpg |>
    group_by(manufacturer) |>
    summarise(hwy = mean(hwy), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(delta = hwy - mean(hwy), manufacturer = reorder(manufacturer, delta))
md <- max(abs(mk$delta))
ggplot(mk, aes(delta, manufacturer, fill = delta)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.62) +
    scale_fill_chanwe_div(limits = c(-md, md)) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Highway MPG vs fleet average",
            eyebrow = "DIVERGING - BARS"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Above average in green, below in vermillion"
        ),
        x = "Δ MPG",
        y = NULL,
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::mpg")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(legend_position = "none")
```

# The Signed System

One pair everywhere: `chanwe_palette("signed")` drives the KPI arrows,
table deltas and the diverging poles. `direction` states the movement
(▲/▼); `valence` states whether that movement is good news and drives the
color.

::::: {.kpi-grid cols="4"}
:::: {.kpi title="POSITIVE" main="#147705" main-color="#147705" secondary="hue-true brand green" direction="none"}
::::
:::: {.kpi title="NEGATIVE" main="#CC1914" main-color="#CC1914" secondary="hue-true vermillion" direction="none"}
::::
:::: {.kpi title="NEUTRAL" main="#666666" main-color="#666666" secondary="brand ink-03" direction="none"}
::::
:::: {.kpi title="CONTRAST" main="4.9+" unit=":1" secondary="on all five surfaces" direction="up"}
::::
:::::

## KPI scoreboard with valence

```{r}
#| label: kpi-valence
#| fig-height: 4.4
ggplot(econ, aes(date, unemp_pct)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = chart[["chart-blue"]]) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Unemployment rate",
            eyebrow = "SIGNED - KPI SCOREBOARD"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Share of population, monthly",
            kpi = chanwe_kpi(
                num = "3,9",
                label = "PCT",
                period = "APR·2015",
                mtc1_num = "0,1pp",
                mtc1_label = "MoM",
                mtc1_direction = "-",
                mtc1_valence = "good",
                mtc2_num = "0,4pp",
                mtc2_label = "QoQ",
                mtc2_direction = "-",
                mtc2_valence = "good",
                mtc3_num = "1,1pp",
                mtc3_label = "YoY",
                mtc3_direction = "+",
                mtc3_valence = "bad"
            )
        ),
        x = NULL,
        y = "%",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::economics")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

## Signed deltas in tables

`chanwe_col_signed()` colors by the column's *raw* values; `flip` marks
the smaller-is-better rows so color reads as valence, not sign.

```{r}
#| label: table-signed
smaller_is_better <- deltas$metric %in% c("Opex", "Churn")
chanwe_kbl(
    deltas,
    title = "Quarterly performance",
    subtitle = "Signed deltas via chanwe_col_signed() - flip marks Opex and Churn so color reads as valence",
    eyebrow = "SIGNED - TABLES",
    caption = "Source: finance close, Q1 - simulated",
    col_labels = c(
        metric = "Metric",
        actual = "USD K",
        qoq = "QoQ",
        yoy = "YoY"
    ),
    stub = "metric",
    fmt = list(
        actual = function(x) {
            formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ",")
        },
        qoq = function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x),
        yoy = function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x)
    ),
    col_colors = list(
        qoq = chanwe_col_signed(flip = smaller_is_better),
        yoy = chanwe_col_signed(flip = smaller_is_better)
    )
)
```

# Header Treatments

The header grammar: mono-caps eyebrow with an orange rule, Archivo title at
1.85x base, Satoshi subtitle, optional note line or KPI scoreboard, and a
`//` source caption.

##### Eyebrow · title · subtitle (default)

```{r}
#| label: hdr-default
#| fig-height: 4.0
p_fleet +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title("Simple fleet view", eyebrow = "HEADER - DEFAULT"),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Eyebrow, title and subtitle with the header rule"
        )
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

##### Subtitle with a note line

```{r}
#| label: hdr-note
#| fig-height: 4.0
p_fleet +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Transmission comparison",
            eyebrow = "HEADER - NOTE LINE"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Linear fit per horsepower band",
            note = "Excludes exotics; n = 32; OLS with no interaction terms"
        )
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

##### KPI scoreboard

```{r}
#| label: hdr-kpi
#| fig-height: 5
p_fleet +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Reservas Internacionales",
            eyebrow = "BCRA · SECTOR EXTERNO"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Evolución de reservas internacionales brutas (USD MM).",
            kpi = kpi_reserves
        )
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white", plot_borders = TRUE)
```

# Surfaces and Frames

`theme_chanwe()` exposes five named surfaces plus `"transparent"` and raw
hex; grid colors adapt per surface.

##### metallic · default

```{r}
#| label: bg-metallic
#| fig-height: 3.8
p_fleet +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "bg_color · metallic · default",
            eyebrow = "SURFACE"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle('theme_chanwe()')
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

##### white

```{r}
#| label: bg-white
#| fig-height: 3.8
p_fleet +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title("bg_color · white", eyebrow = "SURFACE"),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle('theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white")')
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white")
```

## Frames

```{r}
#| label: frame-true
#| fig-height: 3.8
p_fleet +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title("plot_borders · TRUE", eyebrow = "FRAME"),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Thin ink frame lines on the white surface")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(bg_color = "white", plot_borders = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: frame-top-bottom
#| fig-height: 3.8
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.2, color = chart[["chart-teal"]]) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title("plot_borders · top_bottom", eyebrow = "FRAME"),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            'plot_borders = "top_bottom" adds thin ink frame lines'
        ),
        x = "Weight",
        y = "MPG",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(plot_borders = "top_bottom")
```

## Inset figure

::: {.inset-great-figure eyebrow="FY 2025" title="Revenue by Segment" layout="left" position="right" color="beige" source="Data: FY 2025 — valores normalizados"}
La categoría C presenta el valor más alto del conjunto. Los segmentos A y E muestran rendimiento dentro del rango esperado, mientras que F establece el piso de referencia para el análisis diferencial.

```{r}
#| label: inset-facets
p_fleet +
    facet_wrap(~am) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Faceted by transmission",
            eyebrow = "PLOT · INSET"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("title · Archivo  ·  padding · 18pt")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(bg_color = "beige", plot_padding = 18)
```

:::

# Chart Forms

##### Line · direct labels

```{r}
#| label: form-line
#| fig-height: 4.2
ggplot(rev_df, aes(month, revenue, color = segment)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = rev_last, size = 1.9) +
    geom_text(
        data = rev_last,
        aes(y = y_lab, label = segment),
        hjust = 0,
        nudge_x = 7,
        family = "JetBrains Mono",
        size = 6.75 * 0.72 / ggplot2::.pt,
        show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_color_chanwe_d() +
    scale_x_date(
        date_labels = "%b",
        breaks = months[c(2, 5, 8, 11)],
        expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.2))
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Monthly revenue by segment",
            eyebrow = "FORM - LINE"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "Twelve trailing months, USD MM - series labelled where they end"
        ),
        x = NULL,
        y = "USD MM",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: internal ledger, simulated")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe(legend_position = "none")
```

##### Area

```{r}
#| label: form-area
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(econ, aes(date, unemploy / 1000)) +
    geom_area(fill = chart[["chart-coral"]], alpha = 0.85) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title("Unemployed persons", eyebrow = "FORM - AREA"),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Millions, monthly since 2000"),
        x = NULL,
        y = "Millions",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: ggplot2::economics")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

##### Distribution · density

```{r}
#| label: form-density
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(mt, aes(mpg, fill = am)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.7, color = NA) +
    scale_fill_chanwe_d() +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Fuel economy distribution",
            eyebrow = "FORM - DENSITY"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Manual transmissions skew to higher MPG"),
        x = "MPG",
        y = "Density",
        fill = NULL,
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

##### Error bars · mean ± SD

```{r}
#| label: form-errorbar
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(cyl_summary, aes(cyl, avg_mpg)) +
    geom_pointrange(
        aes(ymin = avg_mpg - sd_mpg, ymax = avg_mpg + sd_mpg),
        color = chart[["chart-blue"]],
        linewidth = 0.7,
        size = 0.6
    ) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Fuel economy by cylinders",
            eyebrow = "FORM - ERROR BARS"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Mean ± one standard deviation"),
        x = "Cylinders",
        y = "MPG",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

##### Focus bar · value labels

```{r}
#| label: form-focus
#| fig-height: 4.0
ggplot(cyl_summary, aes(cyl, avg_mpg)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = cyl == "4"), width = 0.62) +
    geom_text(
        aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", avg_mpg)),
        vjust = -0.7,
        family = "JetBrains Mono",
        colour = chanwe_palette("semantic")[["secondary"]],
        size = 6.75 * 0.8 / ggplot2::.pt
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            `TRUE` = chanwe_palette("semantic")[["primary"]],
            `FALSE` = "#D4D4D4"
        ),
        guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Fuel economy by cylinders",
            eyebrow = "FORM - FOCUS BAR"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle(
            "One accent, gray context, values on the bars"
        ),
        x = "Cylinders",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe() +
    theme(
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank()
    )
```

##### Facets

```{r}
#| label: form-facets
#| fig-height: 4.6
ggplot(mt, aes(wt, mpg, color = cyl)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.0) +
    facet_wrap(~am) +
    scale_color_chanwe_d() +
    labs(
        title = chanwe_title(
            "Faceted by transmission",
            eyebrow = "FORM - FACETS"
        ),
        subtitle = chanwe_subtitle("Strip labels in JetBrains Mono Thin"),
        x = "Weight",
        y = "MPG",
        color = "Cyl",
        caption = chanwe_caption("Source: mtcars")
    ) +
    theme_chanwe()
```

# Typst Tables

`chanwe_kbl()` generates native Typst — no HTML-to-PDF translation. Both
densities, every surface, per-column formatting and coloring, stubs,
totals, highlights and vertical rules.

## Surfaces

##### white-ivory · default

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ivory
chanwe_kbl(
    fleet8,
    title = "bg · white-ivory",
    subtitle = "density · spacious",
    eyebrow = "TABLE · SPACIOUS · WHITE-IVORY",
    caption = "Source · Motor Trend, 1974 · mtcars dataset.",
    stub = "model",
    bg = "white-ivory",
    fmt = fmt_fleet
)
```

## Densities and column widths

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spacious-summary
chanwe_kbl(
    cyl_summary |> select(-sd_mpg),
    title = "Fleet summary by cylinder count",
    subtitle = "Spacious density - the presentation default",
    eyebrow = "TABLES - SPACIOUS",
    caption = "Source: mtcars",
    col_labels = c(
        cyl = "Cylinders",
        avg_mpg = "Avg MPG",
        avg_hp = "Avg HP",
        avg_wt = "Avg weight",
        n = "Vehicles"
    ),
    fmt = list(
        avg_mpg = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x),
        avg_hp = function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x),
        avg_wt = function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
    ),
    density = "spacious"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-compact
chanwe_kbl(
    head(mt |> select(model, mpg, cyl, hp, wt, am), 8),
    title = "Vehicle detail",
    subtitle = "Compact density for dense reporting tables - explicit col_widths",
    eyebrow = "TABLES - COMPACT",
    caption = "Source: mtcars",
    col_labels = c(
        model = "Model",
        mpg = "MPG",
        cyl = "Cyl",
        hp = "HP",
        wt = "Weight",
        am = "Transmission"
    ),
    col_widths = c("2.2fr", "1fr", "0.8fr", "1fr", "1.1fr", "1.6fr"),
    fmt = list(
        mpg = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x),
        wt = function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x),
        hp = function(x) sprintf("%.0f", x)
    ),
    stub = "model",
    density = "compact",
    bg = "beige"
)
```

## Totals, highlights and rules

```{r}
#| label: tbl-totals
chanwe_kbl(
    region_rev,
    title = "Revenue by region",
    subtitle = "Total row via n_total; QoQ column highlighted and signed; vline separates quarters from the delta",
    eyebrow = "TABLES - TOTALS + HIGHLIGHT",
    caption = "Source: finance close - simulated",
    col_labels = c(
        region = "Region",
        q1 = "Q1 USD K",
        q2 = "Q2 USD K",
        delta = "QoQ %"
    ),
    stub = "region",
    fmt = list(
        q1 = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
        q2 = function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","),
        delta = function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x)
    ),
    col_colors = list(delta = chanwe_col_signed()),
    n_total = 1,
    highlight_cols = 4,
    vlines = 3,
    bg = "white-ivory"
)
```

::: {.chanwe-callout kind="success" eyebrow="ONE SYSTEM" title="The same tokens, everywhere"}
The QoQ columns above, the KPI arrows and the diverging heatmap poles are
the exact same three hexes — `chanwe_palette("signed")`. Change them once
and every chart, table and report follows.
:::
